facts.statement: The genus Herrerasaurus was first described by Osvaldo Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.statement: The name Herrerasaurus means "Herrera's lizard" and honors the rancher who found the first specimen in 1958 in South America.
facts.quote: Its name means "Herrera's lizard", after the rancher who discovered the first specimen in 1958 in South America.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Herrerasaurus come from the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina, dating to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 231.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: All known fossils of this carnivore have been discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation of Carnian age (late Triassic according to the ICS, dated to 231.4 million years ago) in northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus measured about 6 meters in length and weighed approximately 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Measuring 6 m long and weighing around 350 kg, this genus was one of the earliest dinosaurs from the fossil record.

facts.statement: Osvaldo Reig named the genus after Victorino Herrera, a goatherd who discovered fossils near San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.

facts.statement: Following the discovery of a nearly complete skeleton in 1988, most phylogenies classify Herrerasaurus as an early saurischian.
facts.quote: However, with the discovery of an almost complete skeleton and skull in 1988, Herrerasaurus has been classified as an early saurischian in most of the phylogenies on the origin and early evolution of dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus belongs to the family Herrerasauridae, which includes some of the earliest genera in dinosaur evolution.
facts.quote: It is a member of the Herrerasauridae, a family of similar genera that were among the earliest of the dinosaurian evolutionary radiation.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno argued that Herrerasaurus should be classified as a primitive theropod.
facts.quote: However, Sereno favored classifying Herrerasaurus (and the Herrerasauridae) as primitive theropods.

facts.statement: There is a persistent scientific debate regarding whether Herrerasaurus is a basal saurischian or a primitive theropod, with different researchers supporting each view.
facts.quote: These two classifications have become the most persistent, with Rauhut (2003) and Bittencourt and Kellner (2004) favoring the early theropod hypothesis, and Max Langer (2004), Langer and Benton (2006), and Randall Irmis and his coauthors (2007) favoring the basal saurischian hypothesis.

facts.statement: If Herrerasaurus is a theropod, it suggests that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged before the middle Carnian and independently evolved features like an advanced ankle joint.
facts.quote: If Herrerasaurus were indeed a theropod, it would indicate that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged even earlier than herrerasaurids, before the middle Carnian, and that "all three lineages independently evolved several dinosaurian features, such as a more advanced ankle joint or an open acetabulum".

facts.statement: Ischisaurus cattoi and Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis are considered synonyms of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Ischisaurus cattoiReig, 1963 Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensisNovas, 1986

facts.statement: Adult Herrerasaurus reached a total length of up to 6 meters, a skull length of 56 centimeters, and a weight of 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adults had skulls up to 56 cm long and were up to 6 m in total length and 350 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Smaller specimens of Herrerasaurus measured approximately 4.5 meters in length and weighed about 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Smaller specimens were about 4.5 m long and weighed about 200 kg.

facts.statement: The outer toes of Herrerasaurus were small, with the first toe possessing a small claw.
facts.quote: The outer toes (I and V) were small; the first toe had a small claw.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a tail partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections that balanced the body and aided in speed.
facts.quote: The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was also an adaptation for speed.

facts.statement: The first two fingers and the thumb of Herrerasaurus ended in curved, sharp claws used for grasping prey.
facts.quote: The first two fingers and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grasping prey.

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth digits of Herrerasaurus were small stubs without claws.
facts.quote: The fourth and fifth digits were small stubs without claws.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a pelvis similar to saurischian dinosaurs, but with a bony acetabulum that was only partially open.
facts.quote: Its pelvis is like that of saurischian dinosaurs, but it has a bony acetabulum (where the femur meets the pelvis) that was only partially open.

facts.statement: The ilium of Herrerasaurus was supported by only two sacrals, which is considered a basal trait.
facts.quote: The ilium, the main hip bone, is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait.

facts.statement: The pubis of Herrerasaurus pointed backwards, a derived trait also seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.
facts.quote: However, the pubis points backwards, a derived trait as seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.

facts.statement: The end of the pubis in Herrerasaurus had a booted shape like avetheropods, and its vertebral centra had an hourglass shape found in Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Additionally, the end of the pubis has a booted shape, like those in avetheropods; and the vertebral centra have an hourglass shape as found in Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a long, narrow skull lacking most specializations of later dinosaurs, resembling primitive archosaurs like Euparkeria.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus had a long, narrow skull that lacked nearly all the specializations that characterized later dinosaurs, and more closely resembled those of more primitive archosaurs such as Euparkeria.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had five pairs of skull openings, two pairs of which were for the eyes and nostrils.
facts.quote: It had five pairs of fenestrae (skull openings) in its skull, two pairs of which were for the eyes and nostrils.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had jaws equipped with large serrated teeth for eating flesh and a slender, flexible neck.
facts.quote: The jaws were equipped with large serrated teeth for biting and eating flesh, and the neck was slender and flexible.

facts.statement: According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus is distinguished by features including a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, a ridge on the jugal bone, a deeply incised supratemporal fossa, a subquadrate ventral squamosal process with a lateral depression, a quadratojugal bone overlapping the quadrate face, an inturned pterygoid process, a slender ribbed dentary process, a forked surangular bone, a humerus with a proximally projected internal tuberosity separated by a deep groove, enlarged hands measuring 60% of the humerus plus radius size, and a humeral entepicondyle with anterior and posterior depressions.
facts.quote: According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features: the presence of a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, and the dorsal part of laterotemporal fenestra is less than a third as wide as the ventral part; the presence of a ridge on the lateral surface of the jugal bone, and a deeply incised supratemporal fossa that extends across the medial postorbital process; the subquadrate ventral squamosal process has a lateral depression, and the quadratojugal bone overlaps the posterodorsal quadrate face; the pterygoid process of the quadrate has an inturned, trough-shaped ventral margin, and the presence of a slender ribbed posterodorsal dentary process; the surangular bone has a forked anterior process for articulation with the posterodorsal dentary process; the humerus' internal tuberosity is proximally projected and separated from the humeral head by a deep groove (also present in coelophysoids); possesses enlarged hands, which are 60% of the size of the humerus+radius, and the humeral entepicondyle is ridge-like with anterior and posterior depressions; and the posterior border of the ilial peduncle forms a right angle with the dorsal border of the shaft on the ischium.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was originally classified within the Carnosauria, a group that included animals similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus was originally considered to be a genus within Carnosauria, which then included forms similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus

facts.statement: Romer (1966) classified Herrerasaurus as a prosauropod possibly within Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Romer (1966), simply noted that Herrerasaurus was a prosauropod possibly within Plateosauridae

facts.statement: Benedetto (1973) named the family Herrerasauridae for Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus, classifying them as Saurischians possibly within Theropoda but not Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: Benedetto in 1973, who named for the taxa the new family Herrerasauridae, which he classified as saurischians, possibly within Theropoda but not in Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Galton (1977) proposed that Herrerasauridae included only Herrerasaurus and classified it as Saurischian incertae sedis.
facts.quote: In 1977 Galton proposed that Herrerasauridae only included Herrerasaurus, and found it to be Saurischian incertae sedis

facts.statement: Brinkman and Sues (1987) considered Herrerasaurus basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia while still placing it inside Dinosauria.
facts.quote: Proposed in 1987 by Brinkman and Sues, Herrerasaurus has at times been considered basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia, although Brinkmann and Sues still considered it to be inside Dinosauria

facts.statement: Novas (1996) supported a theropod position for Herrerasaurus, placing it closer to Neotheropoda than Eoraptor or Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: In 1996, Novas went further by supporting a theropod position for Herrerasaurus with a phylogenetic analysis, which placed it closer to Neotheropoda than Eoraptor or Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Langer (2004) found it more likely that Herrerasaurus was a basal Saurischian rather than a theropod or non-dinosaurian.
facts.quote: Langer (2004) conducted a phylogenetic analysis, and found that it was much more likely that Herrerasaurus was a basal saurischian, than either a theropod or a non-dinosaurian

facts.statement: Bittencourt et al. (2014) placed Herrerasauridae in a polytomy with Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha, with Eoraptor also in an unresolved position.
facts.quote: A more recent analysis, by Bittencourt et al. (2014), placed Herrerasauridae in a polytomy with Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha, with Eoraptor also being in an unresolved position

facts.statement: Martinez et al. (2011) placed Eoraptor within Sauropodomorpha, Herrerasauridae as the most basal theropods, and Eodromaeus as the next most basal in a phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: In 2011, Martinez et al. described Eodromaeus, a basal theropod from the same formation as Herrerasaurus. In a phylogenetic analysis, Eoraptor was placed within Sauropodomorpha, Herrerasauridae was placed as the most basal theropods, and Eodromaeus was placed as the next most basal

facts.statement: Chindesaurus and possibly Caseosaurus may be members of the Herrerasauridae clade, though their relationships are not fully understood and are debated.
facts.quote: Other members of the clade may include Chindesaurus from the Upper Petrified Forest (Chinle Formation) of Arizona, and possibly Caseosaurus from the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas, although the relationships of these animals are not fully understood, and not all paleontologists agree

facts.statement: Alwalkeria and Teyuwasu might be related to Herrerasaurus as possible basal theropods.
facts.quote: Other possible basal theropods, Alwalkeria from the Late Triassic Lower Maleri Formation of India, and Teyuwasu, known from very fragmentary remains from the Late Triassic of Brazil, might be related

facts.statement: Paul (1988) noted that the suggestion that Staurikosaurus pricei was a juvenile Herrerasaurus was incorrect.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) noted that it had been incorrectly suggested that Staurikosaurus pricei was a juvenile Herrerasaurus

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was a carnivore that preyed on small and medium-sized plant eaters based on its teeth and size.
facts.quote: The teeth of Herrerasaurus indicate that it was a carnivore; its size indicates it would have preyed upon small and medium-sized plant eaters

facts.statement: Dental microwear patterns suggest Herrerasaurus may have mainly consumed small prey swallowed whole with minimal oral processing.
facts.quote: The similarity of its dental microwear patterns to those of modern slender-snouted crocodylians and small-bodied broad-snouted crocodylians, however, indicates that Herrerasaurus may have mainly consumed small prey that could have been swallowed whole with very minimal or no oral processing

facts.statement: Coprolites containing small bones but no plant fragments from the Ischigualasto Formation have been assigned to Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: Coprolites (fossilized dung) containing small bones but no trace of plant fragments, discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation, have been assigned to Herrerasaurus based on fossil abundance

facts.statement: Analysis of coprolites suggests that if they belong to Herrerasaurus, the animal could digest bone.
facts.quote: Mineralogical and chemical analysis of these coprolites indicates that if the referral to Herrerasaurus was correct, this carnivore could digest bone

facts.statement: A 2001 study found no signs of stress fractures in 12 hand bones and 20 foot bones of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 12 hand bones and 20 foot bones referred to Herrerasaurus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found

facts.statement: Wounds on a Herrerasaurus skull attributed to bites suggest the animal fought with others, and the wounds were likely caused by a short-lived non-lethal infection.
facts.quote: PVSJ 407, a Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, had a pit in a skull bone attributed by Paul Sereno and Novas to a bite. Two additional pits occurred on the splenial. The areas around these pits are swollen and porous, suggesting the wounds were afflicted by a short-lived non-lethal infection. Because of the size and angles of the wound, it is likely that they were obtained in a fight with another Herrerasaurus

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 2566 was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype of Herrerasaurus (PVL 2566) was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected in 1961 by Victorino Herrera.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1961 by Victorino Herrera

facts.statement: The holotype lived during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, approximately 231 to 229 million years ago.
facts.quote: in sediments that were deposited in the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 231 to 229 million years ago

facts.statement: A.S. Romer discovered specimen MCZ 7063 in 1958, which was originally referred to Staurikosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1958, A.S. Romer discovered specimen MCZ 7063, originally referred to Staurikosaurus in Carnian sediments.

facts.statement: Scaglia collected specimen MACN 18.060 in 1960, which was originally the holotype of Ischisaurus cattoi.
facts.quote: In 1960, Scaglia collected specimen MACN 18.060, originally the holotype of Ischisaurus cattoi, in sediments deposited in the Carnian stage.

facts.statement: More Herrerasaurus specimens were found in the Cancha de Bochas Member in 1990.
facts.quote: In 1990, the Cancha de Bochas Member produced more Herrerasaurus specimens, also from its Carnian beds.

facts.statement: The genus Herrerasaurus was named by Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.quote: species_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.statement: Ischisaurus cattoi and Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis are listed as synonyms of Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Ischisaurus cattoi Reig, 1963 Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis Novas, 1986

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus lived in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 231.4 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Carniense, a principios del período Triásico superior, hace aproximadamente 231,4 millones de años, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: Remains of Herrerasaurus were found in the Valle de la Luna in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en el Valle de la Luna del noroeste de Argentina.

facts.statement: The type species Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis was described by Osvaldo Alfredo Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, fue descrita por Osvaldo Alfredo Reig en 1963

facts.statement: Recent examinations of theropod evolution have classified Herrerasaurus as an early theropod or an early saurischian.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus fue clasificado como un terópodo temprano o un saurisquio temprano en por lo menos cinco exámenes recientes de la evolución de los terópodos

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus is a medium-sized bipedal dinosaur belonging to the family Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio bípedo de tamaño mediano es un miembro de Herrerasauridae

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was a lightly built bipedal carnivore with a long tail and a relatively small head.
facts.quote: era un carnívoro bípedo ligeramente construido con una cola larga y una cabeza relativamente pequeña

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a femur about 50 cm long, a total length of 3 to 6 meters, a hip height of 1.1 meters, and a weight of 210 to 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Presenta un tamaño medio, con el fémur de unos 50 centímetros de longitud, y un largo total de entre 3 y 6 metros, y una altura a las caderas de 1,1 metros, llegando a pesar entre 210 a 350 kilogramos

facts.statement: The largest specimen was initially considered a separate genus, Frenguellisaurus, with a skull measuring about 56 cm long.
facts.quote: El mayor espécimen en un principio fue considerado un género separado, Frenguellisaurus, cuyo cráneo medía unos 56 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: The neck of Herrerasaurus shows no signs of elongation and is quite short and strong.
facts.quote: El cuello del Herrerasaurus no muestra signos de elongación. Es bastante corto y fuerte.

facts.statement: The sacral bone is primitive, consisting of only three vertebrae.
facts.quote: El hueso sacro es primitivo por las pocas vértebras que lo integran, solo tres.

facts.statement: The ilium is supported by only two sacral vertebrae, a basal trait.
facts.quote: El ilion, el hueso principal de la cadera, está soportado por solo dos vértebras sacras, un rasgo basal.

facts.statement: The pubis points backward, a derived trait seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el pubis apunta hacia atrás, un rasgo derivado como se ve en los dromeosáuridos y las aves.

facts.statement: Vegetation included ferns (Cladophlebis), horsetails, and giant conifers (Protojuniperoxylon).
facts.quote: Vegetation consisted of ferns (Cladophlebis), horsetails, and giant conifers (Protojuniperoxylon).

facts.statement: For many years, the classification of Herrerasaurus was unclear, leading to hypotheses that it was a basal theropod, basal sauropodomorph, basal saurischian, or even a non-dinosaur.
facts.quote: Durante muchos años, la clasificación de Herrerasaurus no fue clara, ya que la descripción del animal se basaba en unos pocos restos. Esto conllevó la emisión de diversas hipótesis taxonómicas encuadrándolos como un terópodo basal, un sauropodomorfo basal, un saurisquio basal, o inclusive un no dinosaurio.

facts.statement: A mix of primitive and derived characteristics confused early researchers regarding the systematic position and phylogenetic relationships of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: Posee una mezcla de características primitivas y derivadas que confundieron a los primeros estudiosos de este saurisquio acerca de su posición sistemática y sus relaciones filogenéticas.

facts.statement: Adult Herrerasaurus reached a total length of up to 6 meters and weighed up to 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Los adultos tenían cráneos de hasta 56 centímetros de largo y tenían hasta 6 metros de longitud total y 350 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: The smallest specimens had skulls measuring only 30 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Las muestras más pequeñas tenían la mitad del tamaño, con cráneos de solo 30 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The skull featured a well-developed snout that represented more than half of the skull's length.
facts.quote: Está provisto de una región preorbital, un hocico bien desarrollado, que representa más de la mitad del largo del cráneo.

facts.statement: The skull possessed five pairs of openings, including one pair of eye sockets and one pair of nasal openings.
facts.quote: Posee cinco pares de aberturas en el cráneo, un par son las oculares y otra las abertura nasales.

facts.statement: The upper jaw contained a long row of approximately 20 teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes superiores forman una larga hilera, de unas 20 piezas.

facts.statement: The upper tooth row was completed by about 10 much smaller teeth extending under the eye socket.
facts.quote: La hilera superior de dientes es completada por unas 10 piezas mucho más pequeñas que se extienden hasta debajo de la órbita.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was completely bipedal.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus era completamente bípedo.

facts.statement: It had strong hind limbs with short thighs and fairly long feet, indicating it was likely a fast runner.
facts.quote: Tenía miembros posteriores fuertes con muslos cortos y pies bastante largos, lo que indica que probablemente era un corredor veloz.

facts.statement: The foot had five digits, but only the three middle ones (digits II, III, and IV) supported weight.
facts.quote: El pie tenía cinco dedos, pero solo los tres medios, los dígitos II, III y IV, soportaban peso.

facts.statement: The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was an adaptation for speed.
facts.quote: La cola, parcialmente rígida por las proyecciones vertebrales superpuestas, equilibró el cuerpo y también fue una adaptación para la velocidad.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Herrerasaurus were less than half the length of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores de Herrerasaurus tenían menos de la mitad de la longitud de sus extremidades traseras.

facts.statement: The first two digits and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grasping prey.
facts.quote: Los primeros dos dedos y el pulgar terminaron en garras curvas y afiladas para agarrar la presa.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a flexible joint between the dentary and postdentary bones, allowing it to slide its lower jaw forward and backward to deliver a crushing bite.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus poseía una articulación flexible entre los huesos dentarios y postdentarios, esto permitió que el animal resbalara su quijada inferior hacia adelante y hacia atrás y dar una mordedura de compresión.

facts.statement: Based on these characteristics, it can be inferred that catching and killing prey was the job of the front teeth.
facts.quote: A raíz de estos caracteres se puede inferir que la acción de atrapar y matar a la presa era trabajo de los dientes anteriores.
